absent: Locking and concurrency rules for capability masks and vector maps are not shown in these fragments.
Full layout of the capability descriptor and numeric values of scope and token constants are not shown.
Default scope selection and late processor optionality and panic policy details are not shown.
Firmware operation structure and park loop behavior are not shown.
Sanitised register infrastructure and most matcher implementations are not shown.
Exact boot sequencing and callers of setup, update, enable and verify passes are not shown.

findings.text: Two globally visible helpers manage the native user capability mask. One records a capability index as present. The other reports whether a given index is currently recorded.

A globally visible routine checks the current processor address space identifier width against the boot processor width and aborts on shrinkage. A local helper derives the width from the relevant memory model field, defaulting to the smaller width on unknown encodings.
Early and normal processor termination helpers are visible outside their files for use during bringup failure and hotplug teardown. Both termination helpers never return to the caller.

A globally visible checker validates local vector length support against the system wide map and reports mismatch as an error status, with additional virtualisation related checks when the relevant features are enabled.

The native table declares one entry per user visible hardware capability. Each entry conceptually links a named identification register field and expected value to a kernel capability token under the native type. Optional groups for scalable vector, matrix, branch target, pointer authentication, memory tagging, overlay and guarded stack are included only under corresponding build options. The table ends with an empty sentinel.

The compatibility table declares user visible capabilities for thirty two bit execution. Entries link media and vector, instruction set and security related identification fields to compatibility tokens under two compatibility types. The whole table is present only under the compatibility build option and ends with an empty sentinel.

Neon presence for compatibility requires three media feature subfields of the first vector register to be nonzero. System scope uses a sanitised value while other scopes read the live register. Local scope in a preemptible context triggers a diagnostic.

Recording and querying of user capabilities dispatch on a type tag. Native type updates or tests the native mask. Two compatibility types update or test separate thirty two bit masks. Unknown types trigger a diagnostic and queries report absent.

User capability setup first records unconditional support for identification register access emulation. It then walks the supplied table while entries have a matcher, evaluates each matcher under its default scope and records only those that match.

Capability bringup proceeds through detection, enabling and verification phases distinguished by boot versus later scope. Detection populates system and boot masks. Enabling activates boot scope directly on the boot processor and defers other scopes to a coordinated pass, while later processors enable through local verification. Verification removes or stops processors on unsafe divergence.

Detection iterates the indexed capability pointer array masked to scope. Entries without scope are skipped. Capabilities already recorded are skipped unless they require all processors to match. Match all entries are only set while probing the boot processor and are cleared on later mismatch. Successful matches are recorded in the system mask, logged once when descriptive and not per processor, and additionally recorded in the boot mask when relevant.

Enabling filters the same pointer array by scope and recorded presence. Boot scope entries with an enable callback run directly during boot processor finalisation. Secondary processors obtain boot scope through their own local checks, avoiding costly coordination. Non boot scopes run through a machine wide coordinated call over online processors, whose worker skips boot scope and invokes remaining callbacks.

Local verification compares system wide presence against local matcher outcome for each in scope capability. When the system has a capability the local enable callback still runs even if the local processor lacks it, but missing a non optional capability ends iteration as conflict. When the system lacks a capability, having it locally is a conflict unless explicitly permitted for late processors. Conflicts are reported with processor and capability identity and either panic the kernel or terminate the processor early depending on policy.

Using a smaller address space identifier width than the boot processor is fatal to the whole kernel. Unknown width encodings produce a diagnostic and fall back to the smaller width, which may then trigger the fatal path on processors reporting unknown values.

A secondary processor missing any already advertised native capability is terminated early after a diagnostic. Compatibility capabilities are verified only when thirty two bit user execution is supported. Vector length divergence detected under kernel vector enabled context also terminates the processor early.

Vector verification probes locally supported quanta and requires that every globally required quantum be locally present, otherwise warning and reporting an error. When virtualisation support is present it additionally requires that no locally supported quantum at or below the maximum virtualisable length fall outside the global map, again warning and reporting an error on violation.

Early termination identifies the current processor, logs its refusal to boot, marks it not present, reports it dead to the relevant subsystem, conditionally attempts a firmware stop when hotplug is enabled, records successive boot status values and then enters a park loop.

Normal teardown runs on the departing processor, leaves idle state, masks debug and interrupt state, announces that disposal is safe, delegates shutdown to the per processor firmware operation and never returns, treating return as a fatal error.

Observed uses of the capability descriptor show a matcher callback, a hardware capability type tag and token, scope type bits, a numeric capability index, an optional description and processor mask, and an optional processor enable callback. Table iteration relies on a null matcher sentinel. Detection arrays are indexed by capability number.

Native user capabilities are derived from instruction set attribute, processor feature, memory model, scalable vector, scalable matrix and floating point identification register families. Compatibility capabilities are derived from media, instruction set and processor feature families for thirty two bit support.
The address space identifier width takes values of eight and sixteen bits, selected by the corresponding memory model field. Unknown field values are treated as eight bits.
Early boot verification first checks address space identifier compatibility and then verifies boot scope capabilities on the local processor.
